title: Urban Rooftop Pool Planner
description: Users act as urban architects placing rooftop swimming pools across a virtual city skyline. They must manage a fixed municipal water budget that is conserved across all placed pools — resizing one pool automatically redistributes water volume from others. The planner supports full undo/redo of every placement, resize, and repositioning action.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load VirtualCity.glb as the base city model centered at origin and pool.glb as a clonable asset. Set up a perspective camera at an elevated 45-degree angle overlooking the city with OrbitControls for rotation and zoom. Use a directional light simulating afternoon sun plus ambient light. Implement these interactions: (1) A 'Place Pool' button that clones pool.glb and enters placement mode where the user clicks a rooftop surface via raycasting to position the pool — snap it to the top of the nearest building bounding box. (2) Each placed pool has a draggable handle (TransformControls-style or custom raycasting drag) to reposition it across rooftops. (3) Each pool displays a small floating HTML label showing its current water volume in liters. (4) A global water budget of 500,000 liters is shown in a top HUD bar. When a new pool is placed it receives an equal share — all pools auto-redistribute so total always equals exactly 500,000 (conservation law). (5) Users can click a pool then use a slider to resize it (scale 0.5x to 2.0x); scaling changes that pool's volume proportionally and the remaining budget is redistributed equally among other pools, enforcing conservation. (6) Multi-input coupling: holding Shift while dragging a pool links it to the nearest neighbor pool so both move together. (7) Full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z) tracking every place, move, resize, and delete action. (8) Right-clicking a pool deletes it and redistributes its water to remaining pools. (9) Pools glow blue using emissive material intensity proportional to their water volume percentage. (10) A reset button restores initial state. Minimum 10 distinct interaction steps required to complete a full layout. Display step counter in the HUD.
